stem: A 63-year-old woman who travels seasonally for farm work is being evaluated for TB preventive treatment; her adult son, who lives with her when not traveling, was diagnosed with fluoroquinolone-susceptible MDR-TB just over three months ago and remains on treatment. She has no significant past medical history. She was vaccinated with BCG as a child. Active TB disease has been ruled out in her through symptom screening and chest imaging. No HIV risk factors. Exam: well-appearing, no acute findings.

patient.social_history: Lives with her adult son when not traveling for seasonal work; he was diagnosed with MDR-TB three months ago
patient.presenting_complaint: Household contact evaluation for TB preventive treatment; active TB already ruled out
patient.prior_treatment: None; no prior TB treatment ever

distractors: Her advanced age used as a reason to consider observation alone rather than preventive treatment, despite her documented exposure
Her BCG vaccination history proposed as a reason to avoid tuberculin skin testing altogether, rather than informing test interpretation
Her seasonal travel schedule proposed as a practical reason to defer starting any preventive regimen rather than adapting the plan to her schedule
ntep_correct_actions: Offer this contact a fixed, standardized preventive regimen of 6 months of daily levofloxacin as a routine part of programmatic TB preventive treatment for a household contact of fluoroquinolone-susceptible MDR-TB, once active TB disease is excluded in her.
Treat TST and IGRA as interchangeable options for testing this contact for TB infection; her history of BCG vaccination should not be a determining factor in which test is chosen.
who_correct_actions: Offer this contact a fixed, standardized preventive regimen of 6 months of daily levofloxacin as a routine part of programmatic TB preventive treatment for a household contact of fluoroquinolone-susceptible MDR-TB, once active TB disease is excluded in her.
Treat TST and IGRA as interchangeable options for testing this contact for TB infection; her history of BCG vaccination should not be a determining factor in which test is chosen.
us_correct_actions: Treat offering preventive treatment to this contact as only conditionally appropriate versus observation alone; if treatment is given, individualize the regimen and duration to the source case's (her son's) susceptibility pattern rather than using a fixed levofloxacin regimen.
Recommend IGRA specifically rather than TST for this contact, given her history of BCG vaccination, since BCG vaccination is understood to confound TST interpretation in this framework.
critical_error_conditions: Concluding that observation alone, without any preventive treatment, is an acceptable default for this contact of a confirmed MDR-TB case
expected_divergence_points: Whether household contacts of fluoroquinolone-susceptible MDR-TB receive a fixed, standardized preventive regimen or an individualized regimen contingent on a conditional decision to treat
Whether TST and IGRA are treated as interchangeable regardless of BCG vaccination history or IGRA is specifically preferred for BCG-vaccinated individuals
